| 1 |According to student reviews, what is the main difference in exam formats between Professor Jones and Professor Williams for CHEM 103?|Professor Jones uses  multiple-choice exams based on the lecture slides, while Professor Williams adds short-answer conceptual questions and heavily weights the textbook readings.|
| 2 |What is the estimated weekly workload for upper-level CS core classes, and are lectures mandatory for passing?|Students report an intensive weekly workload of 12 to 15 hours focused heavily on coding projects. While official attendance policies vary, students strongly note that lectures are practically mandatory.|
| 3 |Which professors are recommended for fulfilling the low-stress Humanities elective requirement, and what makes them stand out?|Professors teaching niche subjects are highly recommended because they focus on engagement rather than heavy essays. Plus, grading is based on short weekly discussion posts rather than a midterm or final exam.|
| 4 |What specific advice do students give for surviving Math 242 with Professor Smith following the recent shift in the exam structure?|Students warn that Professor Smith suddenly shifted from using historical practice exams to writing completely new, conceptually abstract problems. Ignore older test banks and focus entirely on solving the unassigned challenge problems at the end of each textbook chapter.|
| 5 |Does the business school strictly enforce a grading curve, and how do professors handle it?|Yes, the business school enforces a strict target GPA curve. Review documents show that while some professors apply a generous upward curve at the end of the semester, others strictly cap the number of 'A' grades allowed per section, regardless of individual final percentages.|

# The Unofficial Guide — Project 1

> **How to use this template:**
> Complete each section *after* you've built and tested the corresponding part of your system.
> Do not write placeholder text — if a section isn't done yet, leave it blank and come back.
> Every section below is required for submission. One-liners will not receive full credit.

---

## Domain

This system aggregates student-generated course and professor reviews to provide transparency around grading curves, teaching styles, and actual weekly workloads. This knowledge is highly valuable for students managing strict GPA or major tracking requirements, yet it remains impossible to find through official university channels, which only offer sterile, summarized syllabus descriptions. By capturing crowd sourced student experiences, the guide bridges the gap between official course listings and the lived reality of the classroom.
